annotation.title_clean: What ethical AI and robots could mean: a conceptual and ethical reflection
annotation.title_en: What ethical AI and robots could mean: a conceptual and ethical reflection
annotation.summary_en: Opinion piece arguing that the ethics of AI and robots should move beyond human-centred analogies and the humanization narrative. It proposes a relational, sociotechnical account of human-AI and human-robot interaction, stressing interdisciplinary work, domain expertise and public engagement. It focuses mainly on conversational AI, with limited attention to embodiment.
key_provisions_or_claims: Humanization narrative creates a normative gap between simulated and real moral capacities.
AI is not a moral agent; human responsibility in design, deployment and governance must be retained.
Human-centred benchmarks for evaluating AI have validity problems.
Ethics should be assessed relationally within sociotechnical practices of interaction and collaboration.
Interdisciplinary work, domain expertise and public engagement are needed for ethical evaluation.
